subject: Biology
why: Version 1 had 26 flat topics, several too broad and two joining topics the syllabus keeps apart. Version 2 moved to parent topics at the grain of the syllabus's numbered topics and subtopics at the grain of its sub-areas. Version 2.1 applies sixteen findings from placing all 46 settled 2025 questions into version 2 with a classifier that did not design it: a scope rule that was wrong, four missing subtopics, five overlapping pairs, five wrong syllabus references, and labels too narrow to show what a subtopic holds. Every one of the 106 legacy database topics is folded in. Nothing in the database is changed by this file.

source.provenance_note: Third-party mirror, file dated 2015-09-24, author field awajis.com. The preamble is WAEC's own standard wording. Not fetched from a WAEC domain directly.
source.scope_rule: The syllabus states that Paper 1, the objective paper, is drawn from Section A. The real 2025 paper also tested Section B content (endocytosis in Q11, DNA in Q45 and Q46) and Section C content (plant life cycles in Q20, population measurement in Q35). So Section A is the spine, and Section B cell biology and Section C content are placed as subtopics, because that is where real questions land. Section B material that no Nigerian paper has been seen to test is left out until one does.

how_to_use: Place a question by what a student must know to answer it, not by words in the stem. A question that mentions a leaf but tests osmosis goes under osmosis. Read the covers line before choosing; where two subtopics look close, the covers line says which one wins.

subtopics.name: Characteristics of living things
subtopics.covers: What separates living from non-living things: the characteristics of life.

subtopics.name: Classification and naming of organisms
subtopics.covers: Kingdoms and major groups, taxonomic ranks, binomial naming, and which group an organism belongs to.

subtopics.name: Differences between plants and animals
subtopics.covers: Features that distinguish plants from animals.

subtopics.name: Levels of organisation
subtopics.covers: Cell, tissue, organ and system levels, with examples of organisms at each.

subtopics.name: Complexity of organisation
subtopics.covers: How complexity increases from single cells to multicellular organisms, and its advantages.

subtopics.name: Forms in which living cells exist
subtopics.covers: Single and free-living, colony, filament, and cells as part of an organism: Amoeba, Volvox, Spirogyra.

subtopics.name: Cell components and their functions
subtopics.covers: Organelles and what each does: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, vacuole, cell wall, chloroplast, membranes.

subtopics.name: Plant and animal cells compared
subtopics.covers: Structures found in one kind of cell and not the other.

subtopics.name: Cell division: mitosis and meiosis
subtopics.covers: Stages of mitosis and meiosis, the cell cycle, and where and why each division happens.

subtopics.name: Diffusion
subtopics.covers: Movement of particles down a concentration gradient, and factors that change its rate.

subtopics.name: Osmosis and plasmolysis
subtopics.covers: Water movement across a membrane; hypotonic, isotonic and hypertonic solutions; turgidity, plasmolysis, crenation and haemolysis.

subtopics.name: Active transport
subtopics.covers: Movement against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration.

subtopics.name: Endocytosis and exocytosis
subtopics.covers: Bulk movement through the membrane: phagocytosis, pinocytosis and exocytosis. Added after 2025 Q11 tested it.

subtopics.name: Skeleton and support in animals
subtopics.covers: Types of skeleton, skeletal materials, bones of the vertebral column and limbs, functions of the skeleton.

subtopics.name: Joints, muscles and movement
subtopics.covers: Types of joint, antagonistic muscles, and how limbs move.

subtopics.name: Supporting tissues in plants
subtopics.covers: Parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma and xylem as supporting tissues, and where each is found. Xylem and phloem as transport vessels go under transport.plants.

subtopics.name: Need for transport
subtopics.covers: Why large organisms need a transport system: surface area to volume ratio and distance.

subtopics.name: Heart, blood vessels and circulation
subtopics.covers: Structure of the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries, and single and double circulation.

subtopics.name: Blood and its functions
subtopics.covers: Composition of blood, what each component does, and the materials blood carries.

subtopics.name: Transport in plants
subtopics.covers: Uptake and movement of water, xylem and phloem as vessels, translocation, and transpiration and the factors affecting it.

subtopics.name: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration
subtopics.covers: Energy release in cells, aerobic against anaerobic respiration, products, fermentation and muscle fatigue.

subtopics.name: Respiratory surfaces and organs
subtopics.covers: Body surface, gills, lungs, tracheal system and leaves as surfaces for gaseous exchange, and their features.

subtopics.name: Mechanism of gaseous exchange
subtopics.covers: Breathing movements, how gases are exchanged at a surface, and the role of stomata.

subtopics.name: Excretory organs and waste products
subtopics.covers: Waste products of metabolism and the organs that remove them, in animals, plants and single cells.

subtopics.name: The kidney
subtopics.covers: Kidney structure, the nephron, how urine is formed, water balance, and kidney disease.

subtopics.name: The liver
subtopics.covers: Liver functions, including making bile, deamination and storage.

subtopics.name: The skin and temperature control
subtopics.covers: Skin structure and how it regulates body temperature.

subtopics.name: The central nervous system
subtopics.covers: Parts of the brain and their functions, and the spinal cord.

subtopics.name: Peripheral and autonomic nervous system
subtopics.covers: Somatic and autonomic systems, sympathetic and parasympathetic effects, and types of neurone.

subtopics.name: Reflex and voluntary actions
subtopics.covers: The reflex arc, reflex against voluntary action, and conditioned reflexes.

subtopics.name: Animal hormones and endocrine glands
subtopics.covers: Endocrine glands, the hormones they make, their effects, and deficiency or excess.

subtopics.name: The eye
subtopics.covers: Structure of the eye, how it forms an image, accommodation, and eye defects and their correction.

subtopics.name: The ear
subtopics.covers: Structure of the ear, hearing and balance.

subtopics.name: Nose, tongue and skin
subtopics.covers: Smell, taste and touch receptors.

subtopics.name: Plant hormones
subtopics.covers: Auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid and ethylene, and their effects.

subtopics.name: Tropisms and nastic responses
subtopics.covers: Growth responses to light, gravity, water and touch, and nastic movements.

subtopics.name: Asexual reproduction
subtopics.covers: Fission, budding, spore formation and vegetative propagation.

subtopics.name: Human reproduction
subtopics.covers: Male and female reproductive systems, gametes, fertilisation, development of the embryo, and birth control.

subtopics.name: Reproduction in animals compared
subtopics.covers: Reproduction across animal groups, internal against external fertilisation, and courtship.

subtopics.name: Flowers and pollination
subtopics.covers: Floral parts and their arrangement, types and agents of pollination, and placentation.

subtopics.name: Fertilisation, fruits and seed dispersal
subtopics.covers: Fertilisation in flowering plants, types and structure of fruits, and agents of dispersal.

subtopics.name: Germination
subtopics.covers: Conditions for germination, epigeal and hypogeal germination, and seed structure.

subtopics.name: Growth and its measurement
subtopics.covers: Aspects of growth, regions of fastest growth, and how growth is measured.

subtopics.name: Metamorphosis and life histories
subtopics.covers: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis, nymphs and larvae, and life cycles of insects and other animals.

subtopics.name: Photosynthesis
subtopics.covers: The process, light and dark reactions, materials and conditions, limiting factors, and experimental evidence.

subtopics.name: Leaf structure
subtopics.covers: External parts of a leaf (apex, margin, lamina, midrib, veins, petiole) and its internal tissues. The leaf is placed here as the organ of photosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Mineral nutrition
subtopics.covers: Macro and micro nutrients, their uses and deficiency symptoms, and the soil and air as sources.

subtopics.name: Food classes and balanced diet
subtopics.covers: Classes of food, their sources and uses, a balanced diet, and deficiency diseases.

subtopics.name: Food tests
subtopics.covers: Tests for starch, sugars, protein and fat, and what a positive result looks like.

subtopics.name: Digestive enzymes
subtopics.covers: Each enzyme, what it acts on, what it produces, where it acts, and the conditions it needs. Sorting rule: a question about what an enzyme does or where it works goes here, not under alimentary.

subtopics.name: Modes of nutrition
subtopics.covers: Autotrophic, holozoic, parasitic, saprophytic and symbiotic nutrition.

subtopics.name: The alimentary system
subtopics.covers: Organs of the gut and associated glands, their structure, and what happens in each region. Sorting rule: a question about an organ's structure or role goes here; one about an enzyme's action goes under enzymes.

subtopics.name: Teeth and dental formula
subtopics.covers: Types of teeth, their structure and functions, and dental formulae of herbivores, carnivores and humans.

subtopics.name: Feeding mechanisms
subtopics.covers: How protozoa, insects and mammals feed, and feeding habits.

subtopics.name: Components of an ecosystem and ecological terms
subtopics.covers: Biotic and abiotic components, and the terms population, community, habitat, niche, biosphere and ecosystem.

subtopics.name: Habitats
subtopics.covers: Aquatic habitats (marine, estuarine, freshwater) and terrestrial habitats, and the organisms typical of each.

subtopics.name: Climatic, topographic and gaseous factors
subtopics.covers: Temperature, light, rainfall, humidity, wind, altitude, slope and gases, and their effect on where organisms live.

subtopics.name: Soil (edaphic) factors
subtopics.covers: Soil composition, texture, water content, pH and air.

subtopics.name: Measuring ecological factors
subtopics.covers: Instruments and methods for measuring temperature, humidity, light, turbidity, salinity, pH and rainfall, such as the Secchi disc, hygrometer and rain gauge.

subtopics.name: Producers, consumers and decomposers
subtopics.covers: Autotrophs and heterotrophs, the trophic roles, and decomposition in nature.

subtopics.name: Food chains and food webs
subtopics.covers: Constructing and reading food chains and webs, and the effect of removing an organism.

subtopics.name: Ecological pyramids
subtopics.covers: Pyramids of numbers, biomass and energy: constructing them and explaining their shapes. Sorting rule: a question about a pyramid's shape or construction goes here.

subtopics.name: Energy transfer and loss
subtopics.covers: How energy passes between trophic levels and how much is lost at each step. Sorting rule: a question about the amount of energy transferred or lost goes here, even if it mentions a pyramid.

subtopics.name: Carbon cycle
subtopics.covers: Movement of carbon through photosynthesis, respiration, decay and combustion.

subtopics.name: Water cycle
subtopics.covers: Evaporation, transpiration, condensation and precipitation.

subtopics.name: Nitrogen cycle
subtopics.covers: Nitrogen fixation, nitrification, denitrification and the bacteria involved.

subtopics.name: Symbiosis and mutualism
subtopics.covers: Associations in which both organisms benefit.

subtopics.name: Parasitism and commensalism
subtopics.covers: Associations in which one benefits and the other is harmed, or unaffected.

subtopics.name: Competition and predation
subtopics.covers: Factors that bring about competition, intra and inter-species competition, and predator and prey.

subtopics.name: Population size and growth
subtopics.covers: Factors that change population size, growth curves and carrying capacity. Sorting rule: a question about why a population changes goes here.

subtopics.name: Ecological succession
subtopics.covers: Primary and secondary succession, pioneer species and climax communities.

subtopics.name: Estimating population size
subtopics.covers: Quadrats, transects, capture and recapture, density, frequency and abundance. Sorting rule: a question about how a population is counted or measured goes here.

subtopics.name: Microorganisms around us
subtopics.covers: Bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa, their structure and where they are found.

subtopics.name: Disease, its transmission and control
subtopics.covers: How diseases spread, carriers and vectors, common diseases, and controlling harmful microorganisms by heat, chemicals and ultraviolet light.

subtopics.name: Immunity and vaccination
subtopics.covers: Natural and artificial immunity, antibodies, and vaccines.

subtopics.name: Useful microorganisms
subtopics.covers: Microorganisms in food production, industry, decay and nitrogen fixation.

subtopics.name: Resources to be conserved
subtopics.covers: Soil, water, wildlife, forests and minerals as resources, renewable and non-renewable.

subtopics.name: Ways of ensuring conservation
subtopics.covers: Reserves, national parks, laws, afforestation, recycling and conservation agencies.

subtopics.name: Pollution
subtopics.covers: Pollution of air, water and soil, its sources and effects, and noise. The syllabus places this under ecological management.

subtopics.name: Continuous and discontinuous variation
subtopics.covers: Variation that grades smoothly (height, weight) against variation in distinct classes (blood group, tongue rolling). Added after 2025 Q41 fell across two subtopics.

subtopics.name: Morphological variation
subtopics.covers: Differences in visible features: height, colour, fingerprints, shape. Sorting rule: when a question asks whether a trait is continuous or discontinuous, use variation.types.

subtopics.name: Physiological variation
subtopics.covers: Differences in body function: tongue rolling, tasting, blood group.

subtopics.name: Uses of variation: crime detection, transfusion, paternity
subtopics.covers: Fingerprints and blood groups used in crime detection, blood transfusion and paternity.

subtopics.name: Genetic terminology
subtopics.covers: Gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, dominant, recessive, homozygous and heterozygous.

subtopics.name: Mendel's laws, crosses and ratios
subtopics.covers: Mendel's laws, monohybrid crosses, Punnett squares, and the ratios and probabilities they give. Probability was merged here: the syllabus does not require probability as a separate calculation, and every cross ends in one.

subtopics.name: Chromosomes, DNA and replication
subtopics.covers: Chromosome structure and number, genes on chromosomes, and DNA structure and replication. Tested in 2025 Q45 and Q46.

subtopics.name: Sex determination, linkage and sex-linked traits
subtopics.covers: How sex is determined, linkage, and sex-linked traits such as haemophilia and colour blindness.

subtopics.name: Applications of heredity
subtopics.covers: Heredity in agriculture and medicine, genetic disorders, mutation, and blood group inheritance.

subtopics.name: Behavioural adaptation in social animals
subtopics.covers: Social organisation in termites, bees and ants, and castes.

subtopics.name: Structural adaptation
subtopics.covers: Structures adapted for obtaining food, protection, securing mates and surviving harsh conditions.

subtopics.name: Adaptive colouration
subtopics.covers: Camouflage, warning colouration and mimicry.

subtopics.name: Evidence of evolution
subtopics.covers: Fossils, comparative anatomy, embryology and geographical distribution.

subtopics.name: Theories of evolution and natural selection
subtopics.covers: Lamarck's use and disuse and inheritance of acquired characters, Darwin's natural selection, and speciation. Natural selection was merged here because Darwin's theory is natural selection.

subtopics.name: Laboratory techniques and safety
subtopics.covers: Handling apparatus and specimens, preserving, and laboratory safety.

subtopics.name: The microscope
subtopics.covers: Parts of the microscope, how to use it, and magnification.

subtopics.name: Biological drawing
subtopics.covers: Rules of biological drawing, labelling and magnification of a drawing.

subtopics.name: Experiments and data handling
subtopics.covers: Experimental design, controls, reading tables and graphs, and drawing conclusions.

subtopics.name: Classifying plants by life span
subtopics.syllabus: C, relevance of biology to agriculture (a)
subtopics.covers: Annuals, biennials and perennials. Split out after 2025 Q20 was hidden inside a broad agriculture label.

subtopics.name: Biology and agriculture
subtopics.syllabus: C, relevance of biology to agriculture
subtopics.covers: Crop improvement, pests and their control, and farming practices.

subtopics.name: Biotechnology
subtopics.covers: Genetic engineering, recombinant DNA, and applied uses of microorganisms.

legacy_note: Each of the 106 legacy database topics is folded into a subtopic where its name is specific, or into a parent topic where it is generic. A question moved to a parent is correct but unplaced within it, and is flagged for reclassification rather than guessed into a subtopic.

v1_to_v2.symbiosis-adaptation: SPLIT: associations (ecology) or adaptation (evolution), decided per question
v1_to_v2.variation-evolution: SPLIT: variation or evolution, decided per question
